title: Transport of normalized tensor constraints through coherent realization
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, and schemes $W$ on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On each small pro-etale site set $B_{W,n}=(\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n)_W$ for $n\ge1$ and $R_W=\lim_n B_{W,n}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Work in the ordinary unbounded derived category $\mathscr D_W=D(\mathscr S(B_{W,\bullet}))$ of whole semilinear systems, with its tensor and geometric inverse image [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. A normalized system has invertible transition adjoints $\alpha^A_{m,n}:q_W^*A_m\to A_n$, where $q_W^*=-\otimes^L_{B_{W,m}}B_{W,n}$, for all $m\ge n\ge1$, with the identity and quotient cocycles [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower]. For systems $A,N$ on $W$ and $C$ on $Y$, write $T_W(A,N)_n=A_n\otimes^L_{B_{W,n}}N_n$, $F_f(C)_n=Lf_n^*C_n$ for $f:X\to Y$, and $U_W=(B_{W,n}[0])_n$, with the induced whole-system transitions.

Write $\mathcal R_WK=(K\otimes^L_{R_W}B_{W,n})_n$ for coherent reduction [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower] and $\mathcal L_W=R\lim\operatorname{Res}$ for total derived limit of the restricted whole system [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Use the canonical adjunction $\mathcal R_W\dashv\mathcal L_W$ and its natural counit $e_A:\mathcal R_W\mathcal L_WA\to A$ [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], invertible for normalized $A$ [lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity]. Let $\widehat T_W,\widehat F_f$ be the actual quotient-complex/Roos completed operations [def-pur-integral-derived-operations].

For finite typed expressions $P$ with input locations and constructors input, coefficient unit, tensor and scheme pullback [def-pur-completed-operation-expressions], let $S_P$ evaluate in $T,F,U$ on normalized inputs, and let $K_P$ evaluate in $\widehat T,\widehat F,\mathcal LU$ on their limits. Define $\beta_P:K_P\to\mathcal L S_P$ recursively by identities at inputs and units, $\beta_{T(P,Q)}=\beta_T(S_P,S_Q)\circ\widehat T(\beta_P,\beta_Q)$ and $\beta_{F_f(P)}=\beta_F(S_P)\circ\widehat F_f(\beta_P)$. Here the primitive maps are those of [lem-pur-completed-primitive-counit-comparison]: the defining quotient realization followed by $\mathcal L T(e_A,e_N)$ and $\mathcal L F_f(e_C)$, respectively. Put $\gamma_P=e_{S_P}\circ\mathcal R(\beta_P)$.

Let $A,N,H$ be arbitrary normalized systems on one $W$. The canonical total-complex maps
$$(x\otimes y)\otimes z\mapsto x\otimes(y\otimes z),\quad b\otimes x\mapsto bx,\quad x\otimes b\mapsto bx,\quad x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{pq}y\otimes x$$
for homogeneous degrees $p,q$ define natural isomorphisms $a:S_P\to S_Q$ of whole systems for the expression pairs $(T(T(A,N),H),T(A,T(N,H)))$, $(T(U_W,A),A)$, $(T(A,U_W),A)$ and $(T(A,N),T(N,A))$, respectively, with each named system regarded as an input expression. They commute with every actual quotient transition. The scalar-extension compatibility is that of the canonical tensor comparison [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence]; for an arbitrary normalized transition the square is composed with naturality in its adjoint $\alpha_{m,n}$. In particular the reassociation routes both take three homogeneous inputs to the tensor of the same three images, the action routes multiply the same scalar, and the symmetry routes retain $(-1)^{pq}$ because scalar factors have degree zero. These claims concern the simultaneous system construction and its flat-term K-flat total representatives, not only the evaluated maps.

Suppose the recursive $\beta_P,\beta_Q$ and their $\gamma$ are invertible. Under these specified comparisons the canonical completed tensor constraint is
$$\widehat a=\beta_Q^{-1}\mathcal L_W(a)\beta_P.$$
This identifies the actual completed quotient-model reassociation, action or signed symmetry with the limit of the displayed system map: inserting the defining counits in the quotient models yields the same total-complex formula, and their naturality permits moving an inserted counit through that formula. Its coherent reduction is the same map, namely
$$\gamma_Q\mathcal R_W(\widehat a)=a\gamma_P,$$
using the whole-system identity $e_{S_Q}\mathcal R_W\mathcal L_W(a)=a e_{S_P}$. Thus both constraint vertices and their arrows, including all quotient transitions and the actual action-unit normalization, are identified.

proof.text: Use the whole-system construction, not independent choices of the evaluated objects. The semilinear system category is the module category of the ring object $B_\bullet$ in the sequence topos. The normalized-operation model gives simultaneous flat-term K-flat models for the finite iterated operations in question, the actual tensor transition adjoints, and their quotient cocycles. In particular $T(A,N)$, $T(N,H)$ and all four source and target systems are normalized. We may calculate tensor constraints on those models, retaining every horizontal system map; no coefficient quotient is assumed flat.

source.place: Tags 07A2 (lemma-tensor-product-K-flat), 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product); simultaneous system application supplied by the cited system-model statements.

proof.text: Apply the ringed-site derived symmetric-monoidal statement on this sequence topos. It supplies natural isomorphisms of whole systems with exactly the displayed reassociation, scalar-action and signed-symmetry formulas. These are the total-complex constraints of the tensor used here. Concretely, on degrees $(p,q,r)$ both reassociated differentials have coefficients $1,(-1)^p,(-1)^{p+q}$; after symmetry the differential coefficients agree since $(-1)^{(p+1)q}=(-1)^{pq+q}$ and $(-1)^p(-1)^{p(q+1)}=(-1)^{pq}$. The ring factor in a unitor has degree zero. The inverse formulas are reverse reassociation, $x\mapsto1\otimes x$, $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, and signed symmetry again. These formulas are taken on the actual sheafified tensor summands of the simultaneous complex models.

source.place: Tag 0FPT (lemma-symmetric-monoidal-derived), with the total-complex formulas and representative normalization of the cited statement.

proof.text: For $m\ge n$ put $q^*=-\otimes^L_{B_m}B_n$. The cochain scalar-extension tensor comparison respects all four constraints. Compose that comparison square with naturality in the actual input adjoints $\alpha^A_{m,n},\alpha^N_{m,n},\alpha^H_{m,n}$. If $\alpha_P,\alpha_Q$ denote the output adjoints specified by the normalized-operation model, the resulting square is $a_n\alpha_P=\alpha_Q q^*(a_m)$. For reassociation both composites send a triple to the same three adjoint images with the same parenthesization. For action both multiply the same scalar after quotienting it. For symmetry both give $(-1)^{pq}$ times the reversed images, since the quotient scalars have degree zero. Composing this square with the scalar-extension units gives the square for the actual semilinear transitions. These are equations of the simultaneous chain constructions and their localizations; they are not deduced from faithfulness of evaluation. The case $m=n$ is the identity square, and composition for $r\ge m\ge n$ uses the input quotient cocycles.

source.place: Tag 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), proof; Tag 03EL (sites-modules-lemma-tensor-product-pullback). Agent expansion for arbitrary transition adjoints.

proof.text:
Suppress $W$, and write $X=\mathcal LA$, $Y=\mathcal LN$, $Z=\mathcal LH$. Write $r_{K,J}:\widehat T(K,J)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal LT(\mathcal RK,\mathcal RJ)$ for the primitive quotient/Roos comparison. Put $D_{A,N}=T(\mathcal RX,\mathcal RY)$, $B_{A,N}=\widehat T(X,Y)$, and $d_{A,N}=e_{D_{A,N}}\mathcal R(r_{X,Y}):\mathcal RB_{A,N}\to D_{A,N}$. Finally put $\delta_{A,N}=e_{T(A,N)}\mathcal R(\beta_{T(A,N)})$. Expanding the specified primitive beta and using counit naturality for $T(e_A,e_N):D_{A,N}\to T(A,N)$ gives the whole-system identity
$$\delta_{A,N}=T(e_A,e_N)d_{A,N}.$$
The same notation and identity apply to $(N,H)$. Each $\delta$ is invertible: its beta is the primitive isomorphism and $T(A,N)$ is normalized, so effectivity makes its counit invertible. Thus $d_{A,N}=T(e_A,e_N)^{-1}\delta_{A,N}$ is invertible as well. No assertion that the counit is monoidal has been used.

source.place: Agent counit calculation using Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok) for the underlying limit model; the adjunction and naturality are the cited system-calculus assertions.

proof.text:
For the associator pair put $V_L=T(\mathcal RB_{A,N},\mathcal RZ)$ and $V_R=T(\mathcal RX,\mathcal RB_{N,H})$. Set $r_L=r_{B_{A,N},Z}$, $r_R=r_{X,B_{N,H}}$, $h_L=T(\delta_{A,N},e_H)$ and $h_R=T(e_A,\delta_{N,H})$. Naturality of $r$ and then of $e$ expands the recursive beta exactly as
$$\beta_P=\mathcal L(h_L)r_L,\qquad \beta_Q=\mathcal L(h_R)r_R.$$
For example naturality moves $\widehat T(\beta_{T(A,N)},1)$ past $r_L$ to $\mathcal LT(\mathcal R\beta_{T(A,N)},1)$, and the subsequent primitive comparison applies $T(e_{T(A,N)},e_H)$, giving $h_L$. The other parenthesization is the same expansion in the second variable.

source.place: Agent expansion of the primitive comparison recursion; counit naturality before evaluation.

proof.text:
Let $a_0:T(D_{A,N},\mathcal RZ)\to T(\mathcal RX,D_{N,H})$ be the total-complex reassociation on the three reduced input systems. The actual quotient-model completed reassociation, after the outer identifications $r_L,r_R$, is obtained by the following explicit roof of system maps:
$$v=T(1,d_{N,H})^{-1}\,a_0\,T(d_{A,N},1):V_L\longrightarrow V_R.$$
Indeed reducing the inner completed tensor gives $\mathcal RB_{A,N}$; its contraction to the tensor of the two reduced inputs is exactly $e_{D_{A,N}}\mathcal Rr_{X,Y}=d_{A,N}$, the scalar-extension adjoint of its total-limit projections. After that contraction the ordinary tensor complex can be reassociated by $a_0$, and the inverse contraction on the right gives $V_R$. Hence the quotient/Roos completed map is $r_R^{-1}\mathcal L(v)r_L$. All arrows in this roof were constructed on whole systems. This describes the actual quotient construction before referring to the desired beta-conjugation identity.

source.place: Agent expansion of quotient-model reassociation; Tags 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), 0FPT (lemma-symmetric-monoidal-derived).

proof.text:
Naturality of reassociation in $e_A,e_N,e_H$, and the identity $\delta=T(e,e)d$, now give
$$h_Rv=T(e_A,T(e_N,e_H))\,a_0\,T(d_{A,N},1)=a\,T(T(e_A,e_N),e_H)\,T(d_{A,N},1)=a h_L.$$
In the first equality $d_{N,H}$ cancels its inverse; the last equality is the corresponding identity for $\delta_{A,N}$. Apply $\mathcal L$ and insert the expansions of beta from the preceding steps. For the actual completed associator this gives $\beta_Q\widehat a=\mathcal L(a)\beta_P$, hence $\widehat a=\beta_Q^{-1}\mathcal L(a)\beta_P$. This is a calculation with the explicit quotient roof, rather than a definition of the completed associator by the last formula.

source.place: Agent reassociation naturality calculation on whole-system morphisms.

proof.text:
For symmetry no inner contraction is present. In the quotient models the completed map is $r_{Y,X}^{-1}\mathcal L(\sigma_0)r_{X,Y}$, where $\sigma_0:T(\mathcal RX,\mathcal RY)\to T(\mathcal RY,\mathcal RX)$ is signed symmetry. Its naturality gives
$$T(e_N,e_A)\sigma_0=\sigma_{A,N}T(e_A,e_N).$$
Together with $\beta_{T(A,N)}=\mathcal LT(e_A,e_N)r_{X,Y}$ and its reversed version, this gives $\beta_Q\widehat\sigma=\mathcal L(\sigma_{A,N})\beta_P$. The sign is the one on the homogeneous tensor summand, and is unchanged by the degree-zero quotient scalar factors.

source.place: Tag 0FPT (lemma-symmetric-monoidal-derived); agent expansion of quotient/Roos symmetry.

proof.text: For the left action put $I=\mathcal LU$. Its actual quotient model first contracts the reduced unit and the reduced input by $T(e_U,e_A):T(\mathcal RI,\mathcal RX)\to T(U,A)$ and then applies the action $\lambda_A:T(U,A)\to A$. Thus its limit map is $\mathcal L(\lambda_AT(e_U,e_A))r_{I,X}=\mathcal L(\lambda_A)\beta_{T(U,A)}$, with target $X=\mathcal LA$. This is the displayed conjugation formula since beta at the input $A$ is the identity. The right action is $\mathcal L(\rho_AT(e_A,e_U))r_{X,I}$ and gives the same equation with $\rho_A$. To check the normalization, $e_U$ at level $n$ is adjoint to the actual projection $I\to\operatorname{Res}B_n[0]$: on an extension tensor $z\otimes b$ it gives $b p_n(z)$. Consequently both action formulas multiply precisely this coefficient with the image of the input; the ring factor is the actual $B_n[0]$ with its element $1$, and no scalar multiple or alternative unit identification is inserted.

source.place: Agent unit calculation, using the scalar-extension adjoint formula and Tag 0FPT (lemma-symmetric-monoidal-derived).

proof.text: The preceding quotient-model descriptions remain valid after replacing any chosen resolution. The well-definedness theorem identifies the actual quotient-complex constructions with their descended functors on flat-term K-flat representatives. The primitive $r$ uses the natural strict Roos comparison $\rho$. For a strict system map $u$ represented by commuting chain maps, the maps $\prod u_n$ commute with $1-s$ and induce the map on the shifted cone; the same equalities therefore hold after applying the Roos construction. Naturality of $\rho$ identifies these maps with $\mathcal L(u)$. Thus the preceding roofs and their equations identify the actual completed functor constraints, not merely separately evaluated arrows or a possibly different limit-model choice.

source.place: Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok), with the strict Roos normalization and descended quotient operations supplied by the cited statements.

proof.text:
For any one of the four pairs, apply the reduction functor to $\beta_Q\widehat a=\mathcal L(a)\beta_P$ and postcompose with $e_{S_Q}$. Counit naturality in the whole-system category gives
$$\gamma_Q\mathcal R(\widehat a)=e_{S_Q}\mathcal R(\mathcal L(a))\mathcal R(\beta_P)=a e_{S_P}\mathcal R(\beta_P)=a\gamma_P.$$
The assumed invertibility of the specified comparisons identifies the vertices as well as the arrows. All factors here are whole-system maps: composing their transition equations proves the transition equation for this equality at every $m\ge n$, including identities and iterated quotients. Naturality in input systems follows from naturality of the tensor constraints, $r$ and $e$ in the same computations. This proves the coherent reduction assertion without asserting that evaluation detects equality of arbitrary morphisms.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NR-d82b182b5 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all 11 steps and every cited statement in full. There are no new nodes, no repair or re-split note, and this is the first delivery. The statement and metadata are kept, proof_deps equals the union of the step uses, and there is no cycle and no SGA. Stacks tags 07A2, 07A4, 0FPT, 0941 and 03EL match their labels, and I read 07A4, 0FPT and 0941. I recomputed the steps. Step 4: delta = T(e_A,e_N) d by counit naturality, and d is invertible by effectivity on T(A,N) together with the primitive beta. Step 5: beta_P = L(T(delta,e_H)) r_L. Step 6: the roof v = T(1,d_NH)^-1 a_0 T(d_AN,1) has the right domains and codomains, and it is the quotient-level construction itself, not defined from the conclusion. Step 7: h_R v = a h_L by naturality of reassociation. Steps 8-9: the symmetry and unit equations follow by naturality. Step 9's normalization z⊗b ↦ b p_n(z) comes from def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower. Step 10: Roos/rho naturality. Step 11: gamma_Q R(â) = a gamma_P. I hand-checked the Koszul signs of Tot reassociation and symmetry, and tested the edge cases: empty site, zero inputs, A=N=H=U, A=N, characteristic 2, unbounded complexes, m=n. The DAG search found no duplicate; the nearest nodes are lem-fix-scalar-completion-associator and lem-pur-expression-counit-substitution-coherence, which are different statements. I accept the six declared off-unit tool uses as generic tools. Two advisories, no change: the sequence topos needs the small site C×N for the ringed-site theorem, and effectivity on D(S(B)) via U_W is inherited from the statement.
